summary: Siskiyou County lookout: a 1922 glass house, then a 1939 BC-301 cab in Shasta-Trinity NF; closed for maintenance in 2008, current status unclear.

facts.design: California Region 4 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 30-foot enclosed timber tower
facts.status_note: The Forest Lookouts page says it was closed for maintenance in 2008; the sources read do not say whether it has reopened.
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Shasta-Trinity National Forest

events.note: Glass lookout house, 14 x 14 ft, on a 30 ft tower, per a July 1922 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Current BC-301 enclosed timber cab built, replacing a Region 5 Plan 4AR cab on an open steel tower; the Register gives 1939 as the built year
Two women stationed at the lookout
A lookout reported her ninth season at the tower
Closed for maintenance; duties transferred to the Siskiyou Bear Lookout (Forest Lookouts only; not confirmed elsewhere)

evidence.supports: administered by US Forest Service, Shasta-Trinity NF
evidence.quote: US Forest Service - Shasta-Trinity National Forest

evidence.supports: current cab built 1939; BC-301 on a 30-foot enclosed timber tower
evidence.quote: The current Black Fox Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1939. The cabin is a California Region 4 Plan BC-301 on a 30 foot enclosed timber tower.

evidence.supports: replaced a Region 5 Plan 4AR cab on an open steel tower
evidence.quote: This structure replaced a California Region 5 Plan 4AR on an open K-brace steel tower.

evidence.supports: July 1922 glass house on a thirty-foot tower
evidence.quote: A glass forest lookout house 14 x 14 feet has just been completed on a thirty-foot tower on Black Fox mountain

evidence.supports: all materials packed in on mules
evidence.quote: All material for the house had to be packed up from the foot of the mountains on mules.
This lookout is on a thirty-foot steel tower
Ed Sanderson has returned from Black Fox mountain, where he has been stationed as lookout.
George Dunlap, who has been stationed at Black Fox lookout station as forest ranger
Misses Billie Burge and Pearl Pursley of Alabama have been stationed on Black Fox lookout.
This is her ninth season as lookout at Black Fox tower.
A bullet severed telephone line disrupted communications in the McCloud ranger district last Saturday night.

evidence.supports: lookout station only means of after-hours contact, 1961
evidence.quote: the Black Fox lookout station is the communication hub for the forest area and is the only means of after hours contact.

evidence.supports: closed for maintenance 2008; duties moved to Siskiyou Bear Lookout

This lookout is on a thirty foot steel tower which commands the country for many miles in all directions.

corrections.why: 152.4 m is 500 feet. The Register describes a 30 foot enclosed timber tower and Forest Lookouts describes a thirty-foot tower, which is 9.1 m.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 152.4 is wrong; 30 ft is 9.1 m (see corrections). The record's 1939 built year is the current BC-301 cab. A July 1922 glass house on a thirty-foot tower is an earlier structure on the same peak; the Register does not say whether the 4AR cab was that house, so the two are not matched. 'Siskiyou Bear Lookout' and the 2008 closure appear only on Forest Lookouts; two searches found nothing on either. Current status and access are not found in any source read, so the story says so and gives no access rule. Only two sources were read. The FFLA California list was grepped, but its layout did not allow reliable registry numbers, so none were taken from it.
